title: Cliff's piano roll on 'Parlor Piano' and his 1960s album
summary: The roll appears on albums of piano rolls, and Cliff's Harlem Banjo-era album recalls 'Hockshop Blues'.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, there's a couple of albums of piano rolls that have the title "Parlor Piano."
That's right, it's on there. And Cliff made an album in the '60s, I guess called "Harlem Banjo" with Elmer Snowden. Elmer Snowden was from Washington, D.C., too.

And on that album he played the "Hockshop Blues" and if you'd listen to the selection on the album which is made in the '60s and the original, it sounds the same. So he didn't vary that much. Once he played a tune, he played it the same way every time and I was remarking that Cliff had small hands and in his style there, the emphasis is on the bass line and he plays quite an intricate bass line and he played inverted thirds, you know, in the chord and he became quite popular because of his stride piano style.
